findings.title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed and remain reusable
findings.body: When the recovery-codes credential lives in a user storage provider (the new federated path introduced by this PR), a successful `credentialManager().isValid(...)` here delegates to the provider's `CredentialInputValidator.isValid`, which can only return true/false. The local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid`, by contrast, removes the used code from the stored credential as part of validation. Nothing in this authenticator (or anywhere else) marks the used code as consumed for the federated case: the subsequent `allCodesUsed()` check re-reads the credential from the user storage via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, which still contains all the codes, so a used recovery code stays valid forever and can be replayed any number of times. Recovery codes are designed as one-time credentials, so this silently downgrades their security whenever they are stored in user storage, and the 'all codes used -> remove credential and force re-configuration' flow never triggers. The new test `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only logs in once with a single code and never asserts that the same code is rejected on a second login, so the regression is not caught. Either the authenticator must consume the code through the SPI (e.g. re-write the credential without the used code) or the SPI contract must clearly require providers to consume one-time codes inside `isValid`, with test coverage for code reuse.

findings.title: Recovery-code login 500s for user-storage users unless the provider overrides the optional getCredentials with a fully-formed hashed model
findings.body: This bean (and `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`) now resolve the credential via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)`, which for federated users relies on `CredentialInputValidator.getCredentials` — a default SPI method that returns an empty stream — and then calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without handling the empty case. A user storage provider that opts into recovery codes the way the SPI documentation suggests for password/OTP — implementing `supportsCredentialType`, `updateCredential` (which receives a plain JSON array of the raw codes as the `UserCredentialModel` challenge response from `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`), and `isValid` — but does not override `getCredentials` will make every recovery-code login page render throw `NoSuchElementException` (HTTP 500). If the provider instead returns the raw `CredentialModel` it stored from `updateCredential`, `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel` throws `IllegalArgumentException` because `secretData` is null and `credentialData` holds the raw JSON array rather than the hashed `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData`/`SecretData` structures. The test provider only works because it re-builds the model through `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`, re-hashing the raw codes on every read — a requirement that is undocumented and inconsistent with the shape handed to the provider on write. The read-side contract for `getCredentials` should be enforced or documented, and the consumers should degrade gracefully when no credential is returned.
